title: Running TermAl host process grows to 27 GiB committed memory within ~1h40m of restart (8 GiB in the last ~4 minutes)
outcome: The cause of the running host's committed-memory growth is identified, from host diagnostics and not guesswork, and fixed or bounded, so a long-running host does not exhaust system commit.
acceptance: A diagnosis note names the component retaining the memory, with evidence: allocation or heap diagnostics, or a reproduction with a measured growth curve. It distinguishes a leak from expected caching.
A fix or bound lands under the standing rule, with a regression test or a measured long-run check showing bounded growth.
A post-restart observation on the installed build shows committed memory stays bounded under ordinary multi-session load.
